changes.old:
watchPositionAsync: jest.fn(),
  removeSubscriptionAsync: jest.fn(),
  reverseGeocodeAsync: jest.fn(),

reason: Installed expo-location resolves watchPositionAsync to a LocationSubscription object with a synchronous remove(): void, but the service stored an old numeric subscription id and called the removed removeSubscriptionAsync API. The service now stores the subscription object, calls remove() synchronously, and clears the handle and tracking flags only after remove() succeeds. If remove() throws, the handle and active flags are preserved so callers see the truthful still-active state and a later stop can retry; once removal succeeds the handle is nulled, so repeated stops do not remove twice. The test double now returns mockSubscription = { remove: jest.fn() } instead of 123, obsolete removeSubscriptionAsync mocking and assertions are replaced, the error case throws from remove() and asserts the service remains active and can retry, and the successful-stop case asserts that a second stop does not call remove again. No test cases were deleted. No new casts, any, suppressions, dependency, config, or native permission changes were introduced. Tests were not executed.

separate_finding.title: Pending start/stop race
separate_finding.detail: startTracking awaits watchPositionAsync before assigning this.watchId and setting isTracking = true. If stopTracking runs while that await is pending, it sees watchId === null, marks the service stopped, and returns. When the pending start resolves it assigns the subscription and sets isTracking = true, resurrecting tracking after stop. Fixing this here would require coordinating in-flight starts, for example with a generation token or pending-start handle, which is outside this contract fix.
separate_finding.suggested_test: Call startTracking without awaiting, immediately await stopTracking, then await the start promise and assert the service is not active and any created subscription was removed.
